articles.title: I wanted ChatGPT and Claude to hand each other tasks, so I connected them to my to-do list
articles.excerpt: I already had an iPhone to-do app. Getting my agents to use a shared list was easier than getting them to start work on their own. I use ChatGPT, Claude, Muse and Grok Bot, sometimes all in the same h…
articles.body: I already had an iPhone to-do app. Getting my agents to use a shared list was easier than getting them to start work on their own. I use ChatGPT, Claude, Muse and Grok Bot, sometimes all in the same hour. When I want one to pick up something another has done, there's no direct way for them to message each other. ChatGPT can't read my Claude chats, and Claude can't ping Grok Bot. I'd already made an iPhone app called Offhand: Voice To Do & Notes. You speak a note and a model on the phone turns it into tasks. It doesn't need an account, and nothing leaves the phone on its own. I wanted a list like that for my agents. So I made Offhand MCP , a remote MCP server at offhandapp.com/mcp. MCP is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.
articles.author: Deyu Wu

articles.body: If you run a computer training centre, typing institute or tally and DTP classes in a small Indian town, your students probably find you through a board outside, a pamphlet or word of mouth. A simple website adds one more way for parents and job seekers to find and trust you. Here is a practical way to plan it without overspending. Start with the questions students actually ask Before thinking about design, list the questions you answer on the phone every day: Which courses do you offer (typing, MS Office, Tally, basic computer, DTP, coding basics)? How long is each course and what are the batch timings? What is the fee, and can it be paid in instalments? Do you give a certificate, and who issues it? The launch of The Sopranos in 1999 paved the way for the 2002 premiere of The Wire , which focused on drug dealers in Baltimore and the police officers trying to disrupt their operations. The series is still one of the best shows of all time, and provided breakout roles for huge stars like Idris Elba and Michael B. Jordan . articles.body: Hi everyone! 👋 I figured it was overdue to introduce myself and join the conversation properly. A bit about me I'm Ed Stuurman, an infrastructure and reliability engineer based in Japan (originally from Europe). My path in tech started in enterprise hardware escalations, debugging kernel dumps, and tracking down CPU microcode bugs at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Since moving to Japan, my focus centered on carrier-grade messaging and distributed systems—scaling email security pipelines, MTAs, and observability systems protecting millions of domains. After daily driving Linux for 15 years (and a Mac for the last 5), Linux and BSD remain the backbone of everything I run—both in production and across my homelab.

articles.title: Retrieval Architecture for Legal Contract Review: Designing Fallbacks That Stay Traceable
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for a legal contract review retrieval architecture, use staged retrieval with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source identifiers carried all the way to the reviewer. A fallbac…
articles.body: Short answer: for a legal contract review retrieval architecture, use staged retrieval with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source identifiers carried all the way to the reviewer. A fallback should widen evidence carefully, never silently replace a tenant's access policy, and should leave a trace of which stage produced each passage. I have been paged for missed jobs and duplicate deliveries, so I treat retrieval like an operational pipeline rather than a single similarity call. In a contract workspace, a missed clause can change a review decision; an over-broad fallback can expose a different client's document.

articles.title: Prompting techniques and their token cost: system prompts, few-shot, chain-of-thought and injection
articles.excerpt: Every word in a prompt is billed, so each technique has a token cost. Here is what the vendors and papers say, with counts I measured using OpenAI's o200k_base tokenizer. My 225-word support-bot promp…
articles.body: Every word in a prompt is billed, so each technique has a token cost. Here is what the vendors and papers say, with counts I measured using OpenAI's o200k_base tokenizer. System prompts are billed on every request My 225-word support-bot prompt is 275 tokens. At 1,000 requests a day that is 8.25M input tokens a month: $16.50 on Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol, $0.825 on Haiku 5.5. It will not cache on its own: Anthropic's minimum cacheable prompt for Sonnet 5.5 is 512 tokens and OpenAI's is 1,024 ( Anthropic prompt caching , OpenAI prompt caching ). To count your own prompts, a browser token counter works without uploading anything.

articles.title: The usual explanation for 50 Ω and 75 Ω coax: three optima, using electrostatic FEM and formulas
articles.excerpt: 50 Ω and 75 Ω are common coaxial-cable impedances. The usual explanation is that there is no single best impedance. For an air-filled coax with a fixed outer diameter, three different goals have three…
articles.body: 50 Ω and 75 Ω are common coaxial-cable impedances. The usual explanation is that there is no single best impedance. For an air-filled coax with a fixed outer diameter, three different goals have three different optima: most power before the dielectric breaks down: 30 Ω most voltage before the dielectric breaks down: 60 Ω lowest conductor loss: 77 Ω 50 Ω is commonly described as a compromise between the first and the last, and 75 Ω as sitting close to the low-loss optimum. For the voltage and power optima, I computed capacitance per metre (which sets Z0) and peak electric field with NovaSolver Studio's electrostatic solver for six inner radii and compared them with formulas. The conductor-attenuation optimum comes from a separate formula.

articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

Google has acknowledged a potentially related issue on its Issue Tracker, but there’s no confirmed fix yet. Google’s big November update packs dozens of bug fixes , but a recent Private Space issue, which unhides the hidden folder in the app drawer, appears to have again slipped through the cracks. For reference, the bug first surfaced following Android 17 QPR1 in September. Fast-forward to Android 17 QPR2 , and the bug is still there. For those unaware, Pixel’s Private Space lets you create a sandbox within your phone.

articles.body: In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. articles.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
articles.excerpt: Every November, I give myself a completely unscientific eyesight test using one of my favorite sights in the night sky — the Pleiades. How many stars can you see?
articles.body: Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
